acceptance.reason: The maintenance evidence at docs/torch-ai-maintenance-status.md:28 records the 1920px light/dark measurements: Hero 1392x897, H1 590x228, API panel 402x316, and the matching Figma node geometry. The implementation encodes the corresponding stable bounds in hero.tsx:74-92 and hero-terminal-demo.tsx:205-211.

theme.css defines the homepage light tokens around #ffffff/#0e0e0e/#2f00e5/#d4ff1f and dark tokens around #1f1f1f/#0e0e0e/#d4ff1f. The section components also apply the required light/dark surfaces and low-opacity borders.

features.tsx:200-206 defines the 1196x470 feature grid with 2x2 235px rows, and features.tsx:223-230 defines four 230px utility cards with md:gap-10 (40px). The 01, 02, 03 labels and CTA/footer rhythm are present; the measured section sequence is documented at docs/torch-ai-maintenance-status.md:28.

The recorded browser matrix in docs/torch-ai-maintenance-status.md:28 states that 1440px, 768px, and 390px light/dark layouts have no real horizontal overflow and stack responsively. The implementation uses responsive grid/flex constraints and overflow clipping.

The maintenance interaction evidence at docs/torch-ai-maintenance-status.md:29 records accessible theme/language/notification controls, mobile menu aria state, Tab reachability, and body scroll locking. public-header.tsx:356-365 exposes the mobile menu's accessible name, aria-expanded, and aria-controls. The administrator URL/HTML/Markdown, section-toggle, template, and override branches remain unchanged in home/index.tsx:71-132 and are preserved by static call-chain review.

The change is limited to the public frontend, theme tokens, i18n, changelog, local assets, and maintenance evidence. No backend API, database, payment, login, or other product contract files are changed.
figma-assets.ts records the required Figma file SnTAn1XXoaAvEQgG61mm38 and nodes 6:2 and 44:2, while the specification records the natural canvas and reference frame dimensions.

The dark homepage uses the required hierarchy, #1f1f1f page surface, #0e0e0e hero/CTA surfaces, low-opacity borders, and neon-lime emphasis in the dark variants of the homepage sections and theme tokens.

The implementation uses the dashboard/model/playground references only to establish shared business theme and navigation semantics. No full rebuild of those business pages is present in the changed paths.

classic-landing.tsx:40-48 renders Hero -> Features plus utility cards -> CTA -> HowItWorks -> Stats -> Footer. This matches the measured Figma hierarchy: the connection CTA is the middle section at y=1999, workflow is y=2529, stats are y=3234, and the dark connection footer begins at y=3804. The phrase dark connection CTA/footer in the acceptance text refers to the final dark footer, not the middle CTA.

theme.css and the section classes provide separate light and dark mappings for white/near-white surfaces, #0e0e0e title/hero/CTA surfaces, #6b6b6b muted text, #2f00e5 purple, #d4ff1f lime, dark #1f1f1f backgrounds, #111/#1c1c1c cards, white text, and low-opacity borders.

features.tsx:200-206 and features.tsx:223-230 encode fixed desktop dimensions, row sizes, card widths, and 40px gaps through stable responsive constraints rather than content-dependent sizing. hero.tsx:74-92, cta.tsx:39, how-it-works.tsx:53, and stats.tsx:77 likewise encode the measured desktop bounds.

The recorded 1440/768/390 light/dark matrix at docs/torch-ai-maintenance-status.md:28 reports no horizontal overflow and responsive stacking. The implementation uses mobile-first single-column behavior and md/lg breakpoints for desktop geometry.

public-header.tsx:255-305 and :356-365 provide named links, visible focus rings, and an accessible mobile menu control. theme-switch.tsx:41-63 provides an accessible theme control and theme-provider.tsx updates the root theme without a full reload. Existing /sign-up, /sign-in, and dashboard navigation contracts are retained.

home/index.tsx:71-132 retains administrator URL iframe, HTML, Markdown, active-template, and per-template content branches. classic-landing.tsx:37-47 retains section visibility toggles and content overrides, with unset values falling back to existing defaults.

All default-home runtime references use repository-local /assets/home-figma paths. The only Figma URLs are sourceUrl provenance metadata in figma-assets.ts; no homepage component imports or references that metadata or a temporary Figma asset URL. Required light/dark export and local SVG assets exist under web/public/assets/home-figma.

The four newly added homepage strings are present in all seven default locales (en, zh, zh-TW, fr, ru, ja, vi), and the corresponding classic locale keys are also present. The 20260820-home-refresh changelog entry is newest-first in web/src/features/changelog/data.ts.

theme.css separates --home-* and --business-* token namespaces. Business defaults retain white/light-gray surfaces and blue, cyan, purple/chart, green, yellow, and red semantic colors, with separate readable dark business surfaces. PublicLayout scopes homepage aliases only to data-public-surface=home.

The changed implementation remains within React 19, TypeScript, Rsbuild, Tailwind, and Base UI. No package or framework upgrade, backend/API/database change, payment/login behavior change, or protected new-api/QuantumNous identifier removal is present.

Recorded Runtime/Builder evidence reports affected oxfmt, oxlint, web tsgo, default production build, classic production build, and git diff --check all passed. Independent read-only checks also passed: oxfmt --check exit 0, affected oxlint exit 0 with only the pre-existing footer no-danger warning, and git diff --check exit 0. No homepage/theme-specific Vitest files exist, so the focused Vitest check was correctly recorded as not applicable.

The maintenance evidence at docs/torch-ai-maintenance-status.md:28-29 records the 1920/1440/768/390 light/dark browser matrix, exact geometry, overflow checks, keyboard/mobile-menu interaction, theme-color synchronization, overlap checks, and no captured console warning/error. This verifier relied on that recorded browser evidence and did not create new browser artifacts.

The classic production build is recorded as passed, local assets and the existing React/Tailwind/Base UI stack are preserved, and protected identifiers remain intact. Administrator custom-home branches remain available through the unchanged home/index.tsx call chain and static review. Authenticated administrator branch-by-branch browser execution remains a documented residual check, not a compatibility failure.

risks: Administrator URL iframe, HTML/Markdown, section-toggle, and content-override branches were preserved and statically reviewed but were not opened one by one in an authenticated administrator browser session; this remains a residual runtime verification item.
No homepage/theme-specific Vitest test files exist, so focused feature tests were not run.
The change is still local to the Comet worktree and has not been committed, merged, pushed, deployed, or online-accepted.
Real production payment, callback, deployment, and other online environment checks remain outside this frontend change.
result.summary: Independent read-only verification passes A1-A22. The measured Figma geometry, responsive matrix, accessible public controls, theme token split, local asset policy, i18n/changelog coverage, custom-home preservation, existing stack, protected identifiers, and recorded Runtime static/browser evidence all satisfy the acceptance criteria. Remaining risks are documented residual administrator-branch browser coverage and normal out-of-scope deployment/online checks.
